steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Combine sweetened condensed milk, key lime juice, and egg yolks in a large bowl; mix well.
Pour mixture into unbaked graham cracker crust.
Bake in the preheated oven until filling is set, about 15 minutes.
Allow to cool completely before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Key Lime Pie
raw_recipe.description: This easy key lime pie is made tart and creamy with yolks, key lime juice, and condensed milk baked in a graham cracker crust for a winning dessert.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Key Lime Pie

Allow to cool completely before slicing.

review.reviewBody: This is the best! Being a Floridian, I have had my share of both very good and very bad Key Lime Pie. I did make a few changes to the recipe after reading the reviews. I only used 4 egg yolks, I used 2 cans sweetened condensed milk, and I used 1 cup key lime juice. Hint**If you can not find any key lime juice then just use equal parts lemon and lime juice (best if fresh). These adjustments will make more filling than needed, but the texture and taste is better. I had to increase my baking time by 15 minutes. I prebaked my redi-crust and this came out great. The new #1 key lime pie for my family.

As other reviewers mentioned, I used 4 egg yolks, 1 cup of lime juice, and 2 cans of sweetened condensed milk. This was just the right amount to fit in the premade pie shell. I then decorated it using whip cream and a pastry bag and garnished with lime wedges. Let's just say, the family was impressed not only with the taste but also with the appearance. Great pie!!!

As written, a four star recipe--with the modifications I made, five star. First, I thought this pie deserved a homemade graham cracker crust, which I baked first, then cooled. Thinking this would be a little too eggy with 5 yolks, I used only four--perfect. I also knew the custard could stand a little more tartness, so I added 1-1/2 tsp. of grated lime zest to the filling. Perfect. I baked it at 350 degrees for 15 minutes, then when cooled, topped the pie with 1 cup of sweetened whipped cream. Light and refreshing citrus-y pie, and the perfect complement to a spicy Mexican meal.

For those of you like me...born without common sense. Thoroughly mix the condensed milk and the lime juice. IN A SEPARATE BOWL...beat the egg yolks until smooth. Take a tbsp of the condensed milk and mix it into the eggs. When combined add another couple spoonfulls to the eggs. Now that your egg mix is no longer bright yellow add it to the big bowl of milk and lime juice...This is what people mean by tempering. If you just dump it all into a bowl together...you get really creamy filling with scrambled egg bits. Lime and egg DO NOT MIX ALONE. The citric acid will "cook" the eggs. Other than that this is a really good recipe:)

I have made this no less than 50 times and it is my most requested recipe! I also use 4 yolks, 1 cup of lime juice (fresh, bottled...sometimes 1/2 lemon, 1/2 lime, you CAN'T go wrong) and 2 cans of sweetened condensed milk, regular or low fat. For the crust I make my own and I think this is the "secret" that makes it a favorite. I put one sleeve of graham crakers (= 1 cup when crushed), 3T sugar, 1t ground ginger and about 1/4 c of coconut, toasted or regular (both work well) in food processor. Combine until graham crackers are fine. If you want more coconut, throw a little more in, but leave as flakes, makes a nice texture for the crust. Mix with 5T of melted butter, press into pie dish or springform and bake for 8-10 mins @ 375. Okay, this may sound crazy, but I promise it works. When I have made dinners for other families, but am rushed on time, I have made two regular crusts and divided the pie filling to make two pies. It truly works! Yes, the pies will be a little less "tall", but it is still great and for those watching their calories, you will have fewer, but still get to have dessert :)

SO DELICIOUS. I read the reviews and made it with 4 egg yolks, 2 cans of sweetened condensed milk, 1/2 cup fresh lime juice + 1/2 cup fresh lemon juice (I didn’t have key limes), and the zest of 2 limes. I baked it for a little over 15 minutes, I think under 20. Pulled it out, let it cool on the counter, then covered it with plastic wrap and put it in the fridge for like 20 hours. Oh my god… it was a crowd pleaser!! And I absolutely loved it. Perfect amount of tartness, according to me and my whole family. Also… make a homemade graham cracker crust. Makes SUCH a difference. I just used 11 graham cracker sheets (crumbed), 2 Tbsp white sugar, 1 Tbsp brown sugar, and 7 Tbsp butter (melted). Pressed it into a pie dish and poured the custard in and baked it. Sooooo delish!! Can’t recommend it enough.

So delicious and super easy peasy to make! I used 4 egg yolks, 3/4 c. of lime juice and 1/4 c. of lemon juice so it can be nice and tart and 2 cans of sweetened condensed milk. I used a 6 oz graham cracker pie crust. Mixed all the ingredients very well and put it in the oven. I had to leave it in for 25 minutes. Next time if I use a bigger pie crust (with a 6 oz crust, the filling went all the way to the top) while the pie is baking, I'll make merigue and then put it on the pie the last 5 minutes. Sooooo good, my family loves it!

6/29/20- I made this recipe again. I used 4 egg yolks, 2 cans of condensed milk and 1 cup of key lime juice. I poured into a homemade unbaked graham cracker crust and baked it at 350 degrees for about 30-35 min. Topped it with some real whipped cream. It also goes great with a homemade raspberry sauce.

I agree with Shrae and copied some of her suggestions. I used 10" pie plate, pre-baked the homemade crust prior then used two 14oz cans of sweetened condensed milk, just 4 yolks (I think they are only for firmness) and just over 1 cup of fresh squeezed lime juice. Once out of the oven I cool in refrigerator, cut, and portion individual slices into 'tupperware' and put in the freezer. Kids LOVE IT.

I loved this tasty pie. I changed 2 things in this recipe not because I didn't like the original recipe but because I thought it would be even better by using 28 oz (2 cans,) of condensed milk and instead of using lime slices to top the pie I took 1/2 pint of heavy whipping cream whipped the cream and used lemon juice in the cream then I piped the cream on the pie after it was cool.

Love the recipe. I did need to cook the pie a little longer - I added 10 min. I added some flaked coconut, and I definitely suggest refrigerating overnight before decorating or serving. Made a huge difference. I love the dense version- but for fun next time I might add some egg white to see if it fluffs it up a bit. So good though- my family loves it.
It was very simple to make, with only a few ingredients needed, and it is was delicious

I’m a guy who doesn’t cook. I’ve never made a pie before but I have a lime tree in a wine barrel that has gone out of control this year. I used 15 limes. Here are the changes I made based on others input: 1. Used store bought pre-made crust that I put in the over for 5 mins before adding filling. 2. Used four yolks not five. 3. Used two cans of condensed milk. 4. Added two tablespoons zest (not using Key limes) 5. One half cup juice PLUS one quarter cup bottled lime juice (because I hadn’t squeezed enough and cheated. 6. Baked eighteen minutes. 7. Put in the fridge overnight. Turned out great. I topped with zest, no whipped cream. Not a fan of the color. I read another recipe where they added green food coloring. Next pie I will use a lemon meringue recipe and switch out for limes. Be sure to get this in the fridge for several hours. You need to eat it cold! PS- just remembered, I added 2 tablespoons of sugar to the mix. BTW, wife not happy. Counts as 28 POINTS on WeightWatchers!!!
Super easy and yummy 😋,need to make everyone!

Love this recipe! I freeze mine since I’m the only one in the family that likes key lime pie! It is delicious when just out of the fridge too but the creamy smoothness is STILL amazing when frozen! I don’t even thaw it! It is so delicious frozen. Like ice cream!!

Great recipe!! I've made it a few times. I've also switched up the juice, it works just as well with fresh lemon juice as it does with the lime juice. I've also done it with a combo of lemon and lime. Made it for my dad's 79th birthday since he's not a cake guy. I did add in 1/2 tsp of my homemade vanilla bean paste as well as a pinch of salt just to bring out the flavors.

I used five yolks, TWO cans of condensed milk, a ready made graham cracker crust, and 3/4 C of Key Lime juice. Turned out fabulous--thanks to SHRAE W for suggesting the second can of condensed milk, the pie held together perfectly and was super creamy. Note: Key Lime juice is super flavorful compared to plain lime juice. (I also scrambled the leftover egg whites and made egg salad!)
Wonderful taste, great consistency, and reminds me of Key West in the winter time. I used three (3) egg yolks rather than five. Works well for us. My kind of recipe, easy, simple, and quick! Love it!
This is the version that I first made in 2004, but it was called 'Easy Key Lime Pie I'. This is probably my go-to pie recipe, especially now that the summer months are here.
My husband's favorite!!
